template.name: Sample Diagnosis Name
symptoms: Describe one visible symptom or field sign.
template.diagnosisMessage: Give a short, plain-language explanation of what the result means.

treatments.name: Sample field action
treatments.description: Describe one low-risk action the farmer can take now.

template.voiceMessage: Give a short spoken explanation of the likely result and the safest next step.

fallback.name: Guidance Unavailable
fallback.diagnosisMessage: This diagnosis does not yet have local guidance in the app.

treatments.name: Mark the affected area
treatments.description: Keep the affected plant or field area marked so it can be checked again.

treatments.name: Avoid accidental spread
treatments.description: Avoid moving cuttings, seed, leaves, or tools from the affected area.

treatments.name: Request local inspection
treatments.description: Ask a local extension agent to inspect the crop before treatment or removal.

fallback.voiceMessage: Guidance is not available for this result. Keep the affected area marked and ask a local extension agent to inspect the crop before treatment or removal.

maize_healthy.name: Healthy Maize
symptoms: No major streaking, lesions, pustules, or wilting
maize_healthy.diagnosisMessage: The maize plant appears healthy according to current image detection. No signs of the diseases currently recognized by this model were detected.
maize_healthy.voiceMessage: Your maize appears healthy according to current image detection. Continue monitoring the crop for unusual spots, streaks, discoloration, or insect damage.

maize_streak_disease.name: Maize Streak Disease
symptoms: Narrow yellow or white streaks running along the leaves
Streaks parallel to the leaf veins
Reduced cob development in severe infections
maize_streak_disease.diagnosisMessage: The maize plant shows signs consistent with Maize Streak Disease.

treatments.name: Remove severely infected plants
treatments.description: Remove severely affected plants where practical to reduce potential sources of infection.
treatments.estimatedCost: Labor intensive, but low-cost if done manually.

treatments.name: Use resistant maize varieties
treatments.description: For future planting, use locally adapted maize varieties with resistance or tolerance to maize streak disease.
treatments.estimatedCost: 7,700 - 10,000 CDF per kg of seed, depending on variety and local availability.

maize_streak_disease.voiceMessage: Your maize may have Maize Streak Disease. This is caused by a virus, so fungicides will not cure it. I can explain low-cost management options.

maize_northern_leaf_blight.name: Northern Leaf Blight
symptoms: Gray-green lesions that later become tan or brown
Large areas of leaves may die during severe infection
maize_northern_leaf_blight.diagnosisMessage: The maize plant shows signs consistent with Northern Leaf Blight.

treatments.name: Manage infected crop residue
treatments.description: Manage infected maize residue after harvest to reduce disease carryover. This can be done by plowing under residue, removing it, or burning it where allowed.

treatments.name: Crop rotation
treatments.description: Rotate maize with suitable non-host crops (root vegetables, legumes, etc.) when practical.
treatments.estimatedCost: Costs depend on the crops chosen for rotation and local market prices. For example, legumes may cost 3,000 - 8,000 CDF per kg of seed (depending on the type of legume), while root vegetables may cost 1,100 - 5,000 CDF per kg of seed.

treatments.name: Plant resistant varieties
treatments.description: Use locally adapted maize varieties with resistance to Northern Leaf Blight.
treatments.estimatedCost: 4,600-9,200 CDF per kg of seed, depending on variety and local availability.

treatments.name: Locally approved fungicide
treatments.description: Fungicide may be considered when disease pressure and expected crop losses justify treatment. Not recommended due to high cost and severe regulations.

maize_northern_leaf_blight.voiceMessage: Your maize may have Northern Leaf Blight. I can give you management options based on your field size and available resources.

maize_common_rust.name: Common Rust
symptoms: Pustules may occur on both sides of the leaf
Leaves may yellow when infection is severe
maize_common_rust.diagnosisMessage: The maize plant shows signs consistent with Common Rust.

treatments.name: Monitor disease spread
treatments.description: Monitor nearby maize plants and determine whether the disease is spreading significantly.

treatments.name: Plant resistant varieties
treatments.description: Use locally adapted rust-resistant maize varieties in future planting.
treatments.estimatedCost: 4,500-9,200 CDF per kg of seed, depending on variety and local availability.

treatments.name: Locally approved fungicide
treatments.description: Fungicide may be considered for severe disease when economically justified. Use only a product registered locally for maize and follow its label.
treatments.estimatedCost: Costs depend on the fungicide used, application method, and local prices. For example, a registered fungicide may cost 15,000 - 30,000 CDF per liter, and application may require additional labor or equipment costs.

maize_common_rust.voiceMessage: Your maize may have Common Rust. Look for small reddish-brown raised spots on the leaves. I can explain your management options.

maize_unknown.name: Unknown Maize Condition
symptoms: Unrecognized changes in leaf color or shape
Spots, streaks, insect damage, or reduced plant growth
Symptoms that do not reliably match the supported maize classes
maize_unknown.diagnosisMessage: The photo appears to show maize, but it does not reliably match the healthy or maize disease classes supported by this model.

treatments.name: Take additional photos
treatments.description: Take clear photos of the whole plant and both sides of affected leaves.

treatments.name: Avoid unconfirmed treatment
treatments.description: Do not apply treatment based only on this result.

treatments.name: Request local inspection
treatments.description: Keep affected plant material separate until a local extension agent can inspect it.

maize_unknown.voiceMessage: I could not identify this maize condition confidently. Take more clear photos and ask a local extension agent to inspect the crop before applying treatment.

cassava_healthy.name: Healthy Cassava
symptoms: No major wilting or stem dieback
cassava_healthy.voiceMessage: Your cassava appears healthy. Continue monitoring the leaves, stems, and roots for unusual changes.

cassava_brown_streak_disease.name: Cassava Brown Streak Disease
symptoms: Yellow or chlorotic patterns on leaves
Brown or dark necrotic areas inside storage roots
Plants may have severe root damage despite limited leaf symptoms
cassava_brown_streak_disease.diagnosisMessage: The cassava plant shows signs consistent with Cassava Brown Streak Disease.

treatments.name: Do not reuse infected cuttings
treatments.description: Avoid using stems from symptomatic plants as planting material.

treatments.name: Use disease-free planting material
treatments.description: Use healthy cassava cuttings from reliable sources.
treatments.estimatedCost: 5,000 - 10,000 CDF per bundle of cuttings (containing 50-100 stems), depending on local availability and variety.

treatments.name: Use resistant or tolerant varieties
treatments.description: Use locally recommended cassava varieties with resistance or tolerance where available.

treatments.name: Remove infected plants
treatments.description: Remove strongly symptomatic plants where recommended and practical to reduce sources of infection.

cassava_brown_streak_disease.voiceMessage: Your cassava may have Cassava Brown Streak Disease. This is a viral disease. Please also photograph the inside of an affected cassava root if possible to further confirm diagnosis. Here are some management options to reduce its spread.

cassava_bacterial_blight.name: Cassava Bacterial Blight
cassava_bacterial_blight.diagnosisMessage: The cassava plant shows signs consistent with Cassava Bacterial Blight.

treatments.name: Use clean planting material
treatments.description: Do not propagate cassava using cuttings from plants showing bacterial blight symptoms.

treatments.name: Remove severely infected material
treatments.description: Remove severely infected plants or plant material where practical.

treatments.name: Sanitize cutting tools
treatments.description: Clean tools used to cut infected cassava before using them on healthy plants. Rinse with water and disinfect with 70%-100% ethanol alcohol if available. Allow to airdry for several minutes before using on healthy plants.
treatments.estimatedCost: Around 2,700 cdf for 1 kg of 85% ethanol alcohol. Costs may vary based on local availability and quantity purchased.

treatments.name: Plant resistant varieties
treatments.description: Use locally adapted varieties with resistance or tolerance where available.
treatments.estimatedCost: 4,600-11,000 CDF per bundle of stems(50-100), depending on variety and local availability. DRC cassava varieties with resistance to bacterial blight may be available for free/subsidized pricing through local agricultural extension services or research institutions.

cassava_bacterial_blight.voiceMessage: Your cassava may have Cassava Bacterial Blight. Avoid using affected plants as planting material and clean cutting tools before using them on healthy plants.

cassava_mosaic_disease.name: Cassava Mosaic Disease
symptoms: Yellow and green mosaic pattern on leaves
cassava_mosaic_disease.diagnosisMessage: The cassava plant shows signs consistent with Cassava Mosaic Disease.

treatments.name: Remove severely infected plants
treatments.description: Remove strongly symptomatic plants where appropriate to reduce sources of infection.

treatments.name: Do not reuse infected stems
treatments.description: Do not take planting cuttings from cassava showing mosaic symptoms.

treatments.name: Use disease-free cuttings
treatments.description: Use healthy planting material from reliable sources.
treatments.estimatedCost: 4,600-11,000 CDF per bundle of stems(50-100), depending on variety and local availability.

treatments.name: Plant resistant varieties
treatments.description: Use locally recommended CMD-resistant cassava varieties where available.
treatments.estimatedCost: 4,600-11,000 CDF per bundle of stems(50-100), depending on variety and local availability. DRC cassava varieties with resistance to bacterial blight may be available for free/subsidized pricing through local agricultural extension services or research institutions.

cassava_mosaic_disease.voiceMessage: Your cassava may have Cassava Mosaic Disease. This disease is caused by a virus, so fungicides will not cure it. Avoid using affected plants for new cuttings. Here are some management options to reduce its spread.

cassava_unknown.name: Unknown Cassava Condition
symptoms: Unrecognized changes in leaf color or shape
Wilting, stem damage, insects, or changes affecting roots
Symptoms that do not reliably match the supported cassava classes
cassava_unknown.diagnosisMessage: The photo appears to show cassava, but it does not reliably match the healthy or cassava disease classes supported by this model.

treatments.name: Take additional photos
treatments.description: Take clear photos of the whole plant, stem, roots when affected, and both sides of affected leaves.

treatments.name: Avoid moving affected cuttings
treatments.description: Do not distribute cuttings or apply treatment based only on this result.

treatments.name: Request local inspection
treatments.description: Keep the plant marked for inspection by a local extension agent.

cassava_unknown.voiceMessage: I could not identify this cassava condition confidently. Take more clear photos and ask a local extension agent to inspect the crop before applying treatment or sharing cuttings.

rice_healthy.name: Healthy Rice
symptoms: No major lesions or yellow mottling
rice_healthy.voiceMessage: Your rice appears healthy. Continue monitoring your crop for unusual spots, yellowing, streaks, or wilting.

rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions near leaf tips or edges
Yellow lesions spreading along the leaf
Young plants may wilt in severe cases
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.diagnosisMessage: The rice plant shows signs consistent with Bacterial Leaf Blight.

treatments.name: Use resistant varieties
treatments.description: Use locally recommended rice varieties resistant or tolerant to bacterial leaf blight.
treatments.estimatedCost: Generally inaccessible for smallholder farmers in DRC, but may be available through local agricultural extension services or research institutions.

treatments.name: Use healthy seed
treatments.description: Plant healthy seed from reliable sources.
treatments.estimatedCost: Standad rice seed costs 4,600-6,000 CDF per kg, depending on variety and local availability.

treatments.name: Avoid excessive nitrogen
treatments.description: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which can increase susceptibility to bacterial leaf blight.
treatments.estimatedCost: Cost difference depends on the previously used fertilizer. Nitrogen fertilizer generally retails for around 80,000-100,000 CDF per 50 kg bag, depending on the type and local availability. Fertilizer with nitrogen generally costs around 100,000 CDF per 50 kg bag.

rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.voiceMessage: Your rice may have Bacterial Leaf Blight. I can explain management options and help estimate their cost.

rice_blast.name: Rice Blast
symptoms: Damage may occur on leaves, nodes, or panicles
Neck infection may prevent grain filling
rice_blast.diagnosisMessage: The rice plant shows signs consistent with Rice Blast.

treatments.name: Use resistant varieties
treatments.description: Plant locally adapted rice varieties with resistance to blast where available.

treatments.name: Avoid excessive nitrogen
treatments.description: Avoid applying excessive nitrogen fertilizer because it can increase blast susceptibility.

treatments.name: Manage infected crop residue
treatments.description: Manage infected rice residue according to locally appropriate practices.

rice_blast.voiceMessage: Your rice may have Rice Blast. I can give you low-cost management options first and then explain other treatments if needed.

rice_yellow_mottle_disease.name: Rice Yellow Mottle Disease
symptoms: Yellow and green mottling of leaves
rice_yellow_mottle_disease.diagnosisMessage: The rice plant shows signs consistent with Rice Yellow Mottle Disease.

treatments.name: Remove severely infected plants
treatments.description: Remove severely affected plants where appropriate to reduce potential sources of infection.

treatments.name: Use resistant varieties
treatments.description: Use locally recommended RYMV-resistant or tolerant rice varieties where available.

treatments.name: Clean agricultural tools
treatments.description: Clean tools and equipment when moving between affected and unaffected rice areas.
treatments.estimatedCost: Around 2,700 cdf for 1 kg of 85% ethanol alcohol. Costs may vary based on local availability and quantity purchased.

rice_yellow_mottle_disease.voiceMessage: Your rice may have Rice Yellow Mottle Disease. This is caused by a virus, so fungicides will not cure it. I can explain ways to limit its spread.

rice_unsupported.name: Rice Diagnosis Not Supported
rice_unsupported.diagnosisMessage: The model grouped this photo as rice, but this checkpoint cannot provide a complete rice diagnosis because two defined rice disease classes are not included in the model.

treatments.name: Do not rely on this model result
treatments.description: Do not treat or remove rice plants based on this unsupported result.

treatments.name: Take additional rice photos
treatments.description: Take clear photos of the whole rice plant, both leaf surfaces, stem base, and panicle when present for review by an expert.

treatments.name: Request local inspection
treatments.description: Ask a local extension agent to inspect the rice before choosing any treatment.

rice_unsupported.voiceMessage: This photo appears to show rice, but the current model does not support a complete rice diagnosis. Ask a local extension agent to inspect the crop before applying treatment.

rice_unknown.name: Unknown Rice Condition
symptoms: Insect damage, unusual plant height, or panicle changes
Symptoms that do not reliably match the supported rice classes
rice_unknown.diagnosisMessage: The photo appears to show rice, but it does not reliably match the healthy or rice disease classes supported by this model.

treatments.name: Take additional photos
treatments.description: Take clear photos of the whole plant, leaf surfaces, stem base, and panicle when present.

treatments.name: Avoid unconfirmed treatment
treatments.description: Do not apply treatment based only on this result.

treatments.name: Request local inspection
treatments.description: Keep affected field areas marked until a local extension agent can inspect them.

rice_unknown.voiceMessage: I could not identify this rice condition confidently. Take more clear photos and ask a local extension agent to inspect the crop before applying treatment.
